data.long_meaning: From the old Cornish language, Jago is derived from the name Iago, which means 'young warrior' or 'yew tree'. This name has been popular in Cornwall for centuries and is now gaining popularity worldwide. The name Jago carries the meaning “Young warrior” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Jago usually hope their child will grow to embody young warrior and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Jago total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

data.cultural_impact: Jago is a name that resonates with the strong and proud cultural heritage of Cornwall, England. It evokes images of brave warriors defending their land and honor, as well as the deep connection to nature represented by the yew tree. Today, people who bear the name Jago can feel a sense of proud history and connection to this unique and ancient region.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Jago also holds spiritual significance, as the Cornish language and mythology were deeply interconnected with the natural world. The name Jago, meaning 'yew tree', represents a connection to the ancestral spirits, as the yew tree was often considered a symbol of the dead and the underworld. Wearing this name can be a reminder of our spiritual connection to the natural world and our ancestors, and a reminder to live a life filled with courage and strength, just like the young warrior represented in the name.
